classification: Seed 262 is (b), a defect, not (a). Row 72 (generation 11, launch 13) named ask-0014 while row 69, then its re-held copy 71, claimed it, and 71 then told it. The only rows that could compose row 72 between steps 215 and 227 are the two start rows that ran at step 222. At that step 69 was leased, and its re-hold moved the claim to 71, so a correct composer could not name ask-0014. Case (a) would need a receipt timeout that gets no copy (superseded, or the re-holds spent), which marks no telling. Here copy 71 was queued and told. The race this round closes by construction: the composer read what nothing claims in one statement and claimed it in a second. Under READ COMMITTED, a second composer reads a claim the first has not committed as no claim and names the decision too; its UPDATE then waits for the first and re-checks the row against a snapshot that cannot see the first's row, so the void-claim test passes and it takes the claim. TestTwoComposersNeverBothNameOneKeptDecision builds that interleaving directly. I did not catch seed 262's exact schedule: 1500 replays and a 1000-seed hunt with a probe did not reproduce it, so the trace's interleaving is built as the two-composer race, not replayed.

proof.criterion: Two composers of one tree never both name one kept decision (seed 262, the architect's ruling (b))
proof.surface: internal/store/kept_decisions_test.go TestTwoComposersNeverBothNameOneKeptDecision on the pod's PostgreSQL 18.6: composer 1 reads, enqueues and claims, uncommitted. Composer 2 starts and is either done or waiting on a lock (pg_locks), and only then does composer 1 commit.

With record/store.go as on edd9ad00 it failed: 'the second composer named [dispatch://LEGION-330/ask/ask-1] while the first claimed dispatch://LEGION-330/ask/ask-1; want nothing named twice'. The fix: UnclaimedKept locks every kept row of the tree, and the tree's readmitted approval, in a statement of its own before it reads. deviations: Seed 262's own schedule was not replayed deterministically; the architect asked for the trace's interleaving as a test, and TestTwoComposersNeverBothNameOneKeptDecision builds the race it reduces to. Seeds 262 and 701 are pinned in keptLongRegressionSeeds.

The lock is a separate SELECT ... FOR UPDATE ahead of the read, rather than one UPDATE ... RETURNING. An UPDATE re-checks a row that another transaction changed against its own start-time snapshot, so its void-claim subquery can still miss the other composer's committed row. Taking the lock first, in a statement of its own, gives the read a snapshot that sees it.
For a spent catch-up reported by an earlier listener after its row finished (claims 0), spentKept writes a fresh catch-up only when the tree has unclaimed decisions, as adoption does.
A catch-up's re-holds can now restart: a holder that never confirms gets a fresh catch-up every cycle of the three re-hold delays, as the architect decided.
